{
  "hypothesis": "Predicted that Chinese readers would obtain preview benefit from the target word (word n+1) when the boundary was located at the end of the character immediately to the left of the target word (character n-1).",
  "design": "within-subjects, 2 (preview type: identical vs. dissimilar) x 2 (boundary location: n-1 vs. n-2)",
  "manipulation_or_predictor": "The preview of the target word was either identical to the target or a dissimilar word, which changed to the target word when the reader's eyes crossed an invisible boundary.",
  "outcome_measure": "First fixation duration, single fixation duration, gaze duration, and skipping probability on the target word.",
  "population_and_setting": "36 native Chinese-speaking undergraduate students from South China Normal University.",
  "sample_size_total": 36,
  "recruitment_and_incentive": "Undergraduate students participating for course credit.",
  "analysis_plan": "Linear mixed models (LMM) for durations and generalized linear mixed models (GLMM) for skipping, with participants and items as crossed random effects.",
  "preregistered_or_confirmatory": "not stated",
  "other_methods_notes": "The study used the gaze-contingent boundary paradigm. The target words were two-character words. The experiment included 48 experimental sentences and 64 filler sentences. Eye movements were monitored at 1000 Hz."
